name: Yulin
tagline: Low-rise lanes packed with cafes, craft beer and live music
description: A grid of 1980s walk-up blocks in Wuhou where the ground floors have all become specialty coffee shops, record bars and hotpot joints. Evenings spill onto the pavement along Yulin Xilu. It is the default base for Chengdu's creative crowd and the easiest place to work from a cafe all day.
bestFor: Freelancers and creatives who want walkable cafe hopping and a real local scene rather than a tower block.
pros: Highest density of laptop-friendly cafes in the city
Old blocks mean cheaper rent than nearby towers
Metro Line 3 and endless cheap food
cons: Bar noise on the main lanes until late
Walk-ups rarely have lifts or good insulation
Apartments are older and can feel damp in winter

name: Chunxi Road and Taikoo Li
tagline: The commercial heart, malls stacked over a Tang dynasty temple
description: Chengdu's central shopping district in Jinjiang, where glass flagship stores wrap around the Daci Temple and the pedestrianised Chunxi Road fills with crowds every evening. Serviced apartments and hotels sit directly above the metro interchange. You pay for the location and the convenience, not for space.
bestFor: Short stayers who want everything within a ten minute walk and a metro line to everywhere else.
pros: Two metro lines cross underneath the district
Coworking, gyms and international food all within walking distance
cons: The busiest and priciest square kilometre in Chengdu
Very little green space or quiet

name: Tongzilin
tagline: Chengdu's long-standing expat pocket, leafy and low-key
description: A quiet residential wedge in south Wuhou lined with plane trees, international schools and a cluster of Western bakeries and wine bars. Buildings are mid-rise with courtyards and compounds. Families and long-term foreign residents settle here because it is calm, green and still only fifteen minutes from the centre.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads and families who want quiet, greenery and English-friendly services.
pros: Genuinely quiet streets and mature tree cover
Established international shops, clinics and schools
Metro Line 1 runs straight into the centre
cons: Rent is above the city average
Nightlife is limited, you travel out for it
Feels sleepy if you want street life

name: Jiuyanqiao and Sichuan University
tagline: Riverside bars next to a huge student campus
description: The stretch of the Jin River around Jiuyanqiao bridge is Chengdu's loudest nightlife strip, backed by the Wangjiang campus of Sichuan University. Cheap noodle shops, print shops and student rentals fill the side streets by day, then the riverside clubs take over after dark.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads and language students who want cheap rent and a young, social crowd.
pros: Some of the cheapest central rents in Chengdu
Endless cheap student food and Mandarin exchange partners
cons: Club noise near the river until 3am
Rental stock is small and worn
Empties out and goes quiet during university holidays

name: Tianfu Software Park and Jiaozi
tagline: Glass towers, tech campuses and new-build apartments
description: The Gaoxin high-tech zone south of the second ring, built around the Tianfu Software Park campuses and the Jiaozi financial towers. Everything is new: wide boulevards, landscaped parks, modern high-rise flats with gyms and parking. It is where Chengdu's tech workforce lives and where coworking floors are cleanest.
bestFor: Remote developers who want new-build comfort, fast fibre and a professional coworking base.
pros: Newest apartment stock with reliable heating and internet
Metro Line 1 plus large landscaped parks
cons: Blocks are big, so you walk far between things
Farther from the old city and its street food
